summary: Priority-weight refill discrepancy after key aliasing causing sustained 429s for enterprise chat+batch mix
description: Issue summary: BrightDesk reports persistent 429s (sustained over several hours) after enabling per-client priority classes and aliasing a legacy API key into their new subaccount. Impact: production chat traffic and scheduled batch summarization jobs are failing intermittently; customer reports increased latency and degraded UX for paid seats. Scope: affects a single enterprise org (BrightDesk) with mixed low-latency chat and long-running batch summarization jobs hitting the same tenant quota. They observed the spike after a planned key-mapping migration at ~2026-03-13 22:00 UTC.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Create two workflows for the same API key: low-latency chat (short calls, high concurrency) and scheduled summarization (bulk requests).
2) Alias legacy key to a subaccount and enable per-client priority weighting (weight=0.2 for batch, 0.8 for chat).
3) Ramp batch jobs to 50 concurrent workers during off-peak and start chat traffic at normal levels.
4) Monitor responses from the API gateway and observe increased 429s starting within 10-15 minutes of aliasing and persisted across refill cycles.
observed_behavior: Persistent 429 responses for chat sessions and bulk summarization requests despite console showing remaining burst credits for the tenant. Token refill metric for the aliased key reports ~10% of expected refill rate.
expected_behavior: After key aliasing and priority-weight config, tenant-level refill should preserve proportional throughput such that chat retains its low-latency target and batch uses remaining capacity without triggering tenant-wide 429s.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-14 02:10 UTC: Support confirmed pattern from BrightDesk logs and collected request IDs (req: bd-rt-1422, bd-batch-4991).
Checked grafana panels: rate_limiter.refill_per_sec and rate_limiter.available_tokens for tenant 8782-brightdesk; observed refill_per_sec for aliased key 'bd-legacy-alias' ~0.07x expected.

Audit: key-alias mapping triggered a code path where per-key refill used the legacy config (per-route default) instead of per-tenant weighted refill; this is a config-mapping mismatch in the priority allocator.
Reviewed recent config deploy: PR github.com/redwood/inference/pull/7682 contained change to alias resolution; unit tests passed but integration test for weighted-refill did not include alias case.

Temp hypothesis: aliasing set the key's effective priority weight to 0.01 during the allocator step, causing refill math to drop token replenishment by ~100x and causing tenant to appear starved despite console burst credits being non-zero.

Checked billing/credit records: no unexpected invoice charge; token accounting visible in console but refill attribution was misattributed to a different subpath (console UI shows credits but backend per-key counter is near-zero).
Ran reproducer in staging with same aliasing steps; reproduced refill delta and 429s within 8 minutes.
mitigation_steps: Applied temporary override to BrightDesk tenant in prod: forced priority-weight mapping for aliased keys to preserve previous weight (override applied at 2026-03-14 03:20 UTC).
Requested BrightDesk to hold scheduled summarization ramp for 2 hours while override observed. Chat 429 rate dropped to baseline within 6 minutes of override.
Opened emergency canary to throttle batch workers: reduced batch concurrency by 60% to avoid retry storms while permanent fix is prepared.
Support note: advised customer to avoid additional aliasing or key-mapping changes until fix shipped.
proposed_fix: Code change to ensure alias resolution path inherits tenant-level priority-weight and refill_rate calculations. Add an integration test covering alias + weighted-priority refill. PR created: github.com/redwood/inference/pull/7698 (in review).
rollout_plan: 1) Merge PR and run canary against subset of enterprise tenants on prod-canary for 30 minutes. 2) Monitor rate_limiter.refill_per_sec and tenant 429 rate dashboards. 3) Gradually roll to remaining regions if metrics stable. 4) Post-deploy, remove temporary override and validate normal refill behavior for aliased keys.
resolution: Workaround (override) applied and reduced customer impact; permanent fix PR in review. Final resolution pending merge and canary rollout.
follow_up_actions: Add integration test for key-alias + priority-weighted-refill to ci/integration.
Update Console UI to clearly surface per-key refill attribution and alias mapping in tenant view.
Run retro with SRE and Product to clarify aliasing behavior in docs and onboarding for enterprise migrations.
Notify BrightDesk success criteria and schedule a short postmortem with customer-facing SRE.
